dining.name: Bar Restaurant

dining.name: Yang's Kitchen

dining.name: Sonmari

dining.name: Bar Di Bello

dining.name: Sushi Note

events.title: Groovers Ball: 3 YEAR ANNIVERSRY (ft. Dance Maniacs, DJ LIGMA, & Oscar Osorio)
events.detail: LA party Groovers Ball turns three with the iconic trio Dance Maniacs, whose irresistible blends of house, breakbeat, electro and East Coast club never fail to move a room.

artist_notes.name: Dance Maniacs
artist_notes.note: LA trio blending house, breakbeat, electro and East Coast club edits — the party's own billing, and an accurate one; more scrappy rave energy than deep-house selectorship.

artist_notes.name: DJ LIGMA
artist_notes.note: Groovers Ball resident (frequently b2b/b3b with Oscar Osorio); part of the crew's hard house/old-school-techno-leaning core since the party's 2023 founding.

artist_notes.name: Oscar Osorio
artist_notes.note: Groovers Ball resident, regularly paired with DJ LIGMA (they've released a joint EP together) — same bangin' rave/techno lane as the rest of the crew.

enrichment.curator_note: This crew runs harder and scrappier than the usual rooftop-vinyl lane — think old-school rave breaks, electro and East Coast club edits over deep grooves; a real following three years in, but it's a Pomona trek for a vibe that's more warehouse than sunset session.
enrichment.description: Groovers Ball's 3rd-anniversary party at Homage Brewing, headlined by house/breakbeat/electro trio Dance Maniacs with residents DJ LIGMA and Oscar Osorio.

artist_notes.name: Stavroz
artist_notes.note: Belgian four-piece live band — organic, cinematic electronic music blending acoustic textures with emotive melodies (breakout tracks 'The Finishing,' 'Gold Town'); Coachella and Pukkelpop alumni, half a million-plus monthly Spotify listeners. A live act, not a DJ set.

enrichment.curator_note: Stavroz play live rather than DJ, so this is closer to the Bonobo/RÜFÜS Du Sol live-electronic lane than a club night — warm, cinematic, built for a room that wants to feel rather than peak. A good pick if you want the melodic-organic end of the taste without the warehouse chase.
enrichment.description: STRANGER THAN presents Stavroz, the Belgian live organic-electronic band, at The Bridge, DTLA, 10pm.

events.detail: Unpredictable club music is the name of the game here, especially with New York's River Moon whose genre-blurring sets span techno, ballroom and beyond.

events.title: HARD Summer Music Festival
events.detail: Open-air fest HARD Summer returns with a globe-trotting line-up boasting Tokischa, salute, Charlotte de Witte, Zack Fox, Shygirl, VTSS and hometown heroes CQUESTT and Dj Warning.

artist_notes.name: Charlotte de Witte
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno powerhouse, KNTXT label boss — hard, hypnotic peak-time techno; a tracked name and one of the strongest bookings on this lineup.

artist_notes.name: Boys Noize
artist_notes.note: Berlin electro/techno veteran (Alex Ridha) — distorted, industrial-leaning club music going back to the mid-2000s Boysnoize Records run; still a reliably weird, high-energy set.

artist_notes.name: Maceo Plex
artist_notes.note: Miami-via-Barcelona producer (Eric Estornel) — tech-house and techno crossover, Ellum Audio boss; deep, dark, groove-driven.

artist_notes.name: Tiga
artist_notes.note: Montreal electro-house institution (Turbo Recordings) — tongue-in-cheek, disco-inflected electro; a real name for the older end of this bill.

artist_notes.name: VTSS
artist_notes.note: Polish DJ/producer on the harder, rave-leaning end of techno — Bicep's Fabric label, T4T LUV NRG co-founder; a genuinely respected underground name amid the festival billing.

artist_notes.name: Shygirl
artist_notes.note: UK rapper/vocalist and NUXXE co-founder — hyperpop-adjacent club music, Sega Bodega/Arca collaborator; more art-club than DJ set.

artist_notes.name: Hannah Laing
artist_notes.note: Scottish DJ/producer on the UK hard-house/hardcore-revival wave — high-BPM, rave-nostalgic tech house.

artist_notes.name: Vintage Culture
artist_notes.note: Brazilian tech-house export, Solotoko boss — tracked name; huge festival draw, big-room but genuinely well-selected house.

artist_notes.name: Mau P
artist_notes.note: Dutch producer of 'Drugs From Amsterdam' fame — tracked name; big-room tech house with a raw, jacking edge.

artist_notes.name: DJ Seinfeld
artist_notes.note: Swedish-Argentine producer (Armand Jakobsson) who pioneered 'lo-fi house' — tracked name; hazy, nostalgic house that's a shade more tasteful than most of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Chris Lorenzo
artist_notes.note: UK bass/house producer, Half Baked label — tracked name; UK garage-inflected, bass-heavy house.

artist_notes.name: Interplanetary Criminal
artist_notes.note: Manchester producer riding the UK bassline/2-step revival — one of the more interesting names on the bill if you like that skippy, rave-adjacent garage sound.

artist_notes.name: Amelie Lens
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno star, Exhale label — tracked name; driving, hypnotic peak-time techno with real European club credibility (see also her own Grand Park date this batch).

artist_notes.name: Andy C
artist_notes.note: UK drum & bass legend, RAM Records boss — outside the house/techno lane but a genuine, decades-deep DJ talent if you catch a set.

artist_notes.name: bahar khadem
artist_notes.note: LA selector behind the Direct Drive party series — a self-described 'Chicago soul' deep house/club-music digger who's shared bills with Ariel Zetina and Introspekt on the DTLA warehouse circuit.

artist_notes.name: Star Eyes
artist_notes.note: NYC-via-LA bass polymath — Trouble & Bass crew co-founder turned Chaos Clan/Warp Mode; jungle, UK garage and Baltimore/Jersey club roots, played Fabric London and Outlook Festival.

artist_notes.name: Etari
artist_notes.note: LA-based (Orange County-raised) producer and AUNTIE co-founder — house through trance and techno, with releases on 100% Silk; regular on the Lights Down Low/HARD Summer circuit.

artist_notes.name: fun2bjane
artist_notes.note: LA DJ (Jane O'Conner) — INCOGNITO and Sensory Signal resident who's played HARD Summer and Skyline; sets bounce between sassy house/techno and late-'90s prog/trance.

artist_notes.name: Shane Thomas
artist_notes.note: LA producer/DJ, Ace Hotel-residency host of the party blush! — experimental house and techno spliced with reggaeton, dancehall and ballroom edits.

artist_notes.name: Nick León
artist_notes.note: Miami producer on TraTraTrax and Future Times — fuses dembow, reggaeton and dancehall rhythm into house/techno (his own coined term: 'arquitectronica'); one of the more genuinely distinctive club producers right now, sun-bleached and heavy in equal measure.

artist_notes.name: Oscar Osorio
artist_notes.note: Groovers Ball resident, regularly paired with DJ LIGMA (they've released a joint EP together) — same bangin' rave/techno lane as the rest of the crew.

artist_notes.name: Pegassi
artist_notes.note: Belgian producer (Sam Huybrecht) running his own label/party series Sweet Nothing — a deliberately 'post-genre' set that swings between trance, techno, eurodance and house rather than staying in a lane. Closer to a big-room selector than a groove/disco DJ.

enrichment.curator_note: This is the maximalist, 68-name-deep HARD Summer bill — Charlotte de Witte, VTSS and Amelie Lens give the techno stage real weight, but the day is mostly festival-scale bass/electro/hyperpop stuff outside the lane. Go for a handful of sets, not the whole grounds.
enrichment.description: Day one of HARD Summer at Hollywood Park Grounds, Inglewood — 60+ act electronic/bass festival lineup including Charlotte de Witte, Amelie Lens, VTSS, DJ Snake, Boys Noize and Zedd.

events.title: HARD Summer Music Festival

artist_notes.name: Knock2
artist_notes.note: US producer straddling bass music and pop-leaning electronic — big festival-stage energy, outside the house/techno lane.

artist_notes.name: Amelie Lens
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno star, Exhale label — tracked name; driving, hypnotic peak-time techno with real European club credibility (see also her own Grand Park date this batch).

artist_notes.name: Andy C
artist_notes.note: UK drum & bass legend, RAM Records boss — outside the house/techno lane but a genuine, decades-deep DJ talent if you catch a set.

artist_notes.name: Tiga
artist_notes.note: Montreal electro-house institution (Turbo Recordings) — tongue-in-cheek, disco-inflected electro; a real name for the older end of this bill.

artist_notes.name: Vintage Culture
artist_notes.note: Brazilian tech-house export, Solotoko boss — tracked name; huge festival draw, big-room but genuinely well-selected house.

artist_notes.name: VTSS
artist_notes.note: Polish DJ/producer on the harder, rave-leaning end of techno — Bicep's Fabric label, T4T LUV NRG co-founder; a genuinely respected underground name amid the festival billing.

artist_notes.name: Boys Noize
artist_notes.note: Berlin electro/techno veteran (Alex Ridha) — distorted, industrial-leaning club music going back to the mid-2000s Boysnoize Records run; still a reliably weird, high-energy set.

enrichment.curator_note: Day two of HARD Summer is the thinner bill for this lane — Amelie Lens and Vintage Culture again, but otherwise skews bass/hyperpop. Only worth it if you're already at the grounds from day one.
enrichment.description: Day two of HARD Summer at Hollywood Park Grounds, Inglewood, with Amelie Lens, Vintage Culture, Zedd, DJ Snake, RL Grime and Boys Noize among others.

artist_notes.name: Fabiano do Nascimento
artist_notes.note: Rio-born, LA-based nylon-string guitarist — Brazilian jazz woven with the city's experimental-jazz crowd (Leaving Records, Far Out, Now-Again); a Tiny Desk alum.

artist_notes.name: John Carroll Kirby
artist_notes.note: LA keyboardist/producer on Stones Throw (My Garden, Septet) — jazz/exotica solo records, plus session work for Frank Ocean, Solange and Steve Lacy.

artist_notes.name: Tiki Pasillas
artist_notes.note: Grammy-nominated SoCal multi-percussionist/drummer with decades of session credits — grounds the rhythm section here.

enrichment.curator_note: This is LA's real jazz-scene network showing up at a bar, not a club night — Fabiano's Brazilian guitar work plus the guy who plays keys for Frank Ocean and Solange makes for a rare, intimate room.

events.title: Post Present Medium    25 Year Anniversary Celebration, Night II…      Gun Outfi
events.detail: Post Present Medium    25 Year Anniversary Celebration, Night II…      Gun Outfit    The Spatulas ‍  ‍ (Bloomington, IN)    Chronophage ‍  ‍ (Austin, TX)    Guiding Light ‍  ‍ (Austin, TX)    Semi Trucks    Muscle Beach      Plus DJ Kate Hall!      7:30 pm    Advance $20 single day tickets available

artist_notes.name: Gun Outfit
artist_notes.note: Olympia-turned-LA psych/post-punk band on Post Present Medium since their 2008 debut EP — a foundational act for the label being celebrated.

artist_notes.name: The Spatulas
artist_notes.note: Bloomington, IN lo-fi punk band on the Post Present Medium roster.

artist_notes.name: Chronophage
artist_notes.note: Austin DIY punk four-piece with a sophisticated, transgressive songwriting bent — two LPs and a run of cassettes deep.

artist_notes.name: Guiding Light
artist_notes.note: Austin punk band singing bilingually in German/English over jangly, hyper-strummed garage — their debut LP just came out on Post Present Medium.

artist_notes.name: Semi Trucks
artist_notes.note: LA art-pop project fronted by Brendan Sepe, grown from a solo bedroom effort into a full band — scrappy, melodic songs.

artist_notes.name: Muscle Beach
artist_notes.note: LA four-piece delivering noisy, scattershot 'party band' improvisations — a Smell regular.

artist_notes.name: Kate Hall
artist_notes.note: No Age/Mika Miko/Dunes-adjacent LA musician (half of the News Feeds project with Luke Fischbeck & Dean Spunt) DJing the night.

enrichment.curator_note: A real DIY institution's 25th birthday at its natural home — Gun Outfit anchors a bill of scrappy touring bands (Spatulas, Chronophage, Guiding Light) that reads like a Post Present Medium family reunion, not a nostalgia cash-grab.
enrichment.description: Post Present Medium's 25th-anniversary all-ages show at The Smell: Gun Outfit, The Spatulas, Chronophage, Guiding Light, Semi Trucks, Muscle Beach, plus DJ Kate Hall, 7:30pm.

artist_notes.name: Andrey Pushkarev
artist_notes.note: Russian DJ/producer (25+ years in) and founder of the Luck of Access label — melodic, melancholic deep house, dub techno and ambient; a genuine deep-selector name, not a festival booking.

artist_notes.name: Taimur
artist_notes.note: NY/Miami-based DJ-producer (Taimur Agha), co-founder of Blkmarket Membership — earned a fabric London debut off the strength of his sets; house-techno crossover with real European club credibility.

enrichment.curator_note: Pushkarev's deep, dubby techno and Taimur's fabric-approved house-techno crossover make this a legit late-night pick if the TBA address comes through — MELT tends to book real selectors over festival names, which is exactly the appeal.

artist_notes.name: John Tejada

artist_notes.note: Certified Groovers resident, LA-based (Puerto Rico-born) — rhythm-forward house/techno selector, also plays as O God / Soundprism.

artist_notes.name: Sky Rivers
artist_notes.note: LA-native DJ since the acid-house '90s, cut his teeth in SF's scene in the 2000s — deep vinyl collector, a Sunday Sessions LA regular too.

artist_notes.name: ZINI (US)
artist_notes.note: LA-based selector (Syrian roots) working the lighter, groove-forward side of house/techno.

events.title: Post Present Medium    25 Year Anniversary Celebration, Night III…      Abe Vigo
events.detail: Post Present Medium    25 Year Anniversary Celebration, Night III…      Abe Vigoda    Callahan & Witscher ‍  ‍ (NYC)    Debt Rag ‍  ‍ (Olympia, WA)    The Intima ‍  ‍ (Portland, OR)    DREAM_MEGA      Plus DJ Cate Kennan!      8:00 pm    Advance $20 single day tickets available    here   .    Advanc

artist_notes.name: Abe Vigoda
artist_notes.note: LA experimental/'tropical punk' band from the mid-2000s Smell scene, on Post Present Medium — jittery, humid, post-punk-meets-tropicalia; this run is a reunion set for the label's anniversary.

artist_notes.name: Callahan & Witscher
artist_notes.note: NYC duo of two veteran underground experimentalists (Jack Callahan, aka die Reihe; Jeff Witscher, aka Rene Hell) whose new project is a surprising, hooky pivot toward songs after years of noise/ambient work.

artist_notes.name: Debt Rag
artist_notes.note: Olympia, WA punk trio (former members of Grass Widow and Girlsperm) playing guitarless, clattering, drum-and-keyboard punk — Post Present Medium's 2023 LP 'Lost to the Fantasy.'

artist_notes.name: The Intima
artist_notes.note: Portland post-punk quartet, violin-driven, active 1999-2004 and recently reunited — shared stages with The Rapture and The Mekons back in the day; PPM reissued their 'Peril and Panic' LP.

enrichment.curator_note: Three nights deep into Post Present Medium's 25th-anniversary run and this one's genuinely stacked — Abe Vigoda's tropical-punk reunion, Callahan & Witscher's weird new pivot into actual songs, and DIY lifers Debt Rag and reunited Portland post-punk act The Intima. This is the Smell's classic guitars-and-noise lane, not the club side of things.
enrichment.description: Night three of The Smell's Post Present Medium 25th-anniversary celebration: reunited LA tropical-punk band Abe Vigoda, experimental duo Callahan & Witscher, Olympia's Debt Rag, and reunited Portland post-punk band The Intima.

events.title: Day Trip In The Park LA: CID, TOBEHONEST, Juos, Cat & Maomi

artist_notes.name: CID
artist_notes.note: Touring tech-house DJ/producer with a run of releases on Lee Foss's Repopulate Mars — big-room but genuinely well-selected festival tech-house, the headliner of this bill.

artist_notes.name: TOBEHONEST
artist_notes.note: LA-based tech-house DJ/producer on the come-up — Latin-groove/hip-hop-inflected sound with Beatport Top 100 releases and cosigns from Chris Lake and John Summit; regular at Exchange LA/Sound/Academy.

artist_notes.name: Juos
artist_notes.note: LA producer working a Latin tech-house lane — reggaeton and Latin rhythmic elements folded into tech-house, festival-circuit booking (Day Trip, Insomniac-adjacent).

artist_notes.name: Cat & Maomi
artist_notes.note: Texas-born, now LA-based DJ duo — sexy, groove-heavy techno/house that's played the Palladium, Sound, EDC and Day Trip; more festival-mainstage than underground selector.

enrichment.curator_note: Day Trip's whole brand is big, sunny, festival-tech-house day parties in the park — fun if you want a rager in the afternoon sun, but this bill skews mainstage-fun over deep selection; go for the vibe, not for discovery.
enrichment.description: Day Trip's outdoor day party at LA State Historic Park with tech-house sets from CID, TOBEHONEST, Juos and Cat & Maomi.

events.title: Sunday Sessions LA: Dylan Payne All Night Long (Vinyl Only)

artist_notes.name: Dylan Payne
artist_notes.note: LA vinyl-only house DJ and Inthebagg label head — deep, tech-house-leaning open-to-close sets; a Sunday Sessions LA regular.

enrichment.curator_note: Sunday Sessions' whole appeal is the format — open-air, one DJ, vinyl only, all night — and Dylan Payne's deep/tech-house crate-digging is a legitimate reason to make the DTLA trip.
enrichment.description: An open-air, vinyl-only all-night set from LA house DJ Dylan Payne, part of the weekly Sunday Sessions LA series.

events.title: Subtract On The Pier Finale - Danny Tenaglia

artist_notes.note: NYC house/techno institution from the Twilo/Vinyl (ex-Sound Factory) era — famous for tribal, driving, hours-long marathon sets that build slow and never let up. A legitimate legend headlining a pier day party.

artist_notes.name: Anton Tumas
artist_notes.note: Subtract Music founder who ran the beloved 'Subtract On The Pier' Long Beach series — deep house/techno/hypnotic-electronica selector, well-regarded in the SoCal underground. This booking is his own series' finale.

enrichment.curator_note: Tenaglia basically invented the template for the marathon tribal-house set, and this closes out Anton Tumas's own pier series — a real send-off, not just another booking, and worth the trip down to Long Beach for that alone.

artist_notes.name: Apache
artist_notes.note: Miami-based, French-born DJ/producer on Abracadabra Records (Miami house/techno label) and founder of the Soundtuary party series — warm, groove-driven house suited to a rooftop-pool crowd.

enrichment.curator_note: A genuine rooftop-pool day party — Apache isn't a name you'll recognize, but Abracadabra's house lane is legit groove, not brostep-adjacent EDM, and the setting alone (2-8pm, DTLA rooftop) is the Sunset-Sessions kind of afternoon you like.
enrichment.description: Daytime rooftop pool party (2-8pm) at Level 8 DTLA headlined by Miami house DJ Apache.

artist_notes.name: Amelie Lens
artist_notes.note: Belgian techno star, Exhale label — tracked name; driving, hypnotic peak-time techno with real European club credibility (see also her own Grand Park date this batch).

artist_notes.name: Anastasia Giovani
artist_notes.note: SoCal-raised, now a fixture of LA's underground techno scene (SXTCY resident, founder of the VSCRL event series) — dark, textured, experimental techno sets.

enrichment.curator_note: A dedicated day-to-dusk Amelie Lens set at Grand Park, not a shared festival stage — genuinely the better way to catch her than the HARD Summer slot the same month. Extended techno-into-acid-into-trance from a real headliner in a proper Factory 93 room.

events.detail: The winner of four 2024 Tony Awards®, including Best Musical, is THE OUTSIDERS.Adapted from S.E. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation."In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of ‘outsiders’ battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self- discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging…and the realization that there is still “lots of good in the world.”

events.title: Bonnie Raitt: Live 2026 with Special Guest Jon Cleary
lineup: Jon Cleary & the Absolute Monster Gentlemen
events.detail: Bluesy singer/songwriter Bonnie Raitt has worked long and hard for her multiple Grammy Awards, hit singles and chart-topping records. Since her 1971 eponymous debut, the California-born performer and long-time activist has steadily maintained a music career, albeit with definite peaks and valleys. The red-headed songstress, one of the only women of her time to play guitar using the bottleneck technique, unleashed seven albums in just nine years, though her big commercial break came with her 10th studio set, 1989’s “Nick of Time.” That 11-track collection, produced by Don Was, earned three Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year. Not only has the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer tackled multiple U.S. tours and international runs, but she’s also a frequent participant in events of social activism, such as Farm Aid and Amnesty International concerts. Raitt’s 16th full-length album and most recent studio release, “Slipstream,” hit retailers in 2012. Not only did ticket sales for the support tour soar, but Raitt also landed the best-selling blues album of the year and took home the Grammy for Best Americana Album.
